auto.empty_hint: Add one directly, or create one quickly from an SSH connection's More menu.
auto.form_hint: Only fields required by this protocol are shown.
auto.name: Name
auto.keep_password: Leave blank to keep the saved password
auto.rdp_password_consent: I understand the risk and allow Terma to pass the saved password to the RDP client
auto.rdp_password_hint: The RDP username and password may be left blank so the client can prompt. After you acknowledge the warning, Windows uses temporary credentials and FreeRDP uses standard input. Because macOS Windows App has no password interface, Terma uses an installed FreeRDP client instead.
auto.vnc_password_hint: A VNC password can be saved in encrypted form, or left blank to be requested when connecting.
auto.xdmcp_resize_hint: Xephyr on Linux and macOS can follow window resizing. Windows opens at the selected initial size and cannot resize reliably. XDMCP/X11 has no universal frame-rate limit.
auto.xdmcp_session_auto: The remote login screen provides the desktop session automatically
auto.xdmcp_local_xserver_required: The device running Terma must have an available local X Server
auto.xdmcp_local_xserver_hint: Linux commonly uses Xephyr, macOS uses XQuartz, and Windows requires an installed and running X Server. XDMCP does not use SSH X11 forwarding, which is not an XDMCP client.
auto.xdmcp_management_hint: The SSH management connection can use a private key, SSH Agent, or password for detection and configuration. The remote display manager authenticates XDMCP graphical sign-in, which normally still requires a desktop username and password.
auto.xdmcp_security_warning: XDMCP is unencrypted and should be used only on a trusted LAN. Use SSH X11, RDP, or VNC across public networks.
auto.ftp_passive_hint: FTP always uses passive mode for compatibility with common NAT and firewall environments.
auto.rdp_display_hint: Automatic mode resizes the RDP desktop with the client window. Fixed mode offers common, ultrawide, 2K, 4K, 5K, 8K, and custom sizes.
auto.rdp_login_user: XRDP signs in with the remote Linux desktop account: {{user}}.
auto.rdp_login_hint: XRDP signs in with the remote Linux desktop account, not a temporary administrator root password, VNC password, or the current Windows account.
auto.xrdp_xorg_hint: Xorg is preferred by default. Xvnc in the login screen is a compatibility backend used only when the Xorg backend is unavailable.
auto.rdp_password_not_admin: Do not enter a temporary administrator password, VNC password, or the current Windows account.
auto.follow_window: Follow window (when supported by the server)
auto.performance_preset_hint: Smooth first lowers JPEG quality to 6 to reduce bandwidth and decode pressure. It does not disable clipboard sync or change the remote resolution.
auto.auto_sync_images_hint: On by default. It works only while automatic clipboard sync is enabled, Terma is in the foreground, and the SSH helper supports images.
auto.vnc_source_summary: Use x11vnc for shared sources and TigerVNC for independent sources
auto.vnc_source_detail: Physical desktops and XRDP sessions are mirrored by x11vnc; TigerVNC creates a separate X11 desktop. Xtigervnc/Xvnc in logs are underlying process names, not another product that needs separate deployment.
auto.vnc_source_risk: RDP, VNC, and XDMCP use different ports. XRDP and TigerVNC under the same Linux user may contend for HOME, DBus, or a single desktop instance; use a separate regular user for independent VNC when possible.
auto.vnc_quality_hint: Image quality controls JPEG compression and is separate from resolution; increasing both usually uses more bandwidth. VNC sends changed regions from the server and has no universal reliable fixed-frame-rate setting.
auto.ssh_clipboard_hint: Used for reliable Chinese clipboard transfer; Linux also needs xclip/xsel or wl-clipboard.
auto.quick_open_enabled_title: Quick open: enabled; open Remote Desktop after detection succeeds
auto.quick_open_disabled_title: Quick open: disabled; open the detection view only
auto.quick_open_enabled_notice: Quick open enabled: Remote Desktop will start automatically after detection succeeds
auto.quick_open_disabled_notice: Quick open disabled: Remote Desktop will remain on the detection view
auto.manual_offline_packages: If neither the remote host nor the local Terma device has network access, download {{packages}} and all dependencies on an online machine with the same distribution, version, and CPU architecture, then upload them through Local Files or SFTP and follow the distribution's offline installation procedure.
auto.manual_offline_components: If neither the remote host nor the local Terma device has network access, download the required components and all dependencies on an online machine with the same distribution, version, and CPU architecture, then upload them through Local Files or SFTP and follow the distribution's offline installation procedure.
auto.manual_commands_unavailable: No commands can be generated automatically for this system. Install the required components manually using the distribution's package-manager documentation.
auto.telnet_warning: Telnet does not encrypt usernames, passwords, or terminal content. Use it only on a trusted network or through an encrypted tunnel.
auto.probe_graphical_login: Inspecting the remote graphical login service
auto.xdmcp_launch_help: Terma starts the local XDMCP window. XDMCP itself does not depend on SSH; the linked SSH connection is used only to inspect and manage the remote display service. Use VNC to share the current desktop.
auto.rdp_launch_help: Terma checks the local client and target TCP port first. SSH is used only for Linux xrdp, desktop-session, and installation management, and does not block Windows or standalone RDP services.
auto.vnc_launch_help: Terma checks the target port and VNC service first. SSH is used only for Linux service and desktop management and does not block standalone {{mode}} VNC connections.
auto.xdmcp_probe_incomplete: The full SSH inspection did not finish, but you can still try the XDMCP graphical login directly
auto.xdmcp_client_required: Install or authorize the local XDMCP client first

reasons.xdmcp_response_invalid: An invalid XDMCP response was received

endpoint_probe.xdmcp_willing: The Terma host received an XDMCP WILLING response from {{endpoint}}. You can start a new graphical login.
endpoint_probe.xdmcp_rejected: {{endpoint}} returned an XDMCP response but is not accepting graphical logins ({{error}}).
endpoint_probe.xdmcp_no_response: {{endpoint}} did not return an XDMCP Query response ({{error}}). A UDP firewall or service policy may discard probes; you can still try a graphical login directly.
endpoint_probe.reachable: The Terma host connected directly to {{endpoint}}. You can start the protocol client; SSH is used only for Linux service management and deeper diagnostics.
endpoint_probe.unreachable: The Terma host could not connect to {{endpoint}} ({{error}}). Check the service, firewall, and network route.

rendering.command_empty: The compatibility launch command is empty
rendering.copy_failed: Failed to copy the compatibility launch command
rendering.rdp_software_display: XRDP {{display}} has fallen back to software rendering
rendering.rdp_software: XRDP graphics acceleration is currently unavailable
rendering.rdp_missing_drm: The DRM device {{device}} configured by xorgxrdp does not exist. Java2D, JavaFX, OpenGL, or embedded-browser interfaces may render blank.
rendering.rdp_software_detail: The xorgxrdp log shows a swrast/software OpenGL fallback. Java2D, JavaFX, OpenGL, or embedded-browser interfaces may render blank.
rendering.rdp_accelerated: XRDP {{display}} detected a DRM render node
rendering.rdp_accelerated_detail: The current log shows no software OpenGL fallback, though individual applications may still be limited by their own graphics backends.
rendering.rdp_pending: XRDP rendering status is waiting for an active session
rendering.rdp_pending_detail: After an RDP graphical session is established, Terma can further inspect DRM and software OpenGL fallback status.
rendering.vnc_macos_shared: VNC is sharing an existing macOS desktop
rendering.vnc_macos_shared_detail: Applications are still rendered by the local desktop session; system Screen Sharing transmits only the final image.
rendering.vnc_xrdp_limited: VNC is sharing the limited XRDP {{display}}
rendering.vnc_xrdp_limited_detail: x11vnc does not change how applications render, so it inherits the source XRDP session's software OpenGL limitations.
rendering.vnc_xrdp_shared_detail: x11vnc directly shares the source XRDP session, so application rendering capabilities match that session.
rendering.vnc_virtual: VNC uses an independent virtual display, which normally provides software rendering only
rendering.vnc_virtual_detail: TigerVNC is not a physical GPU desktop. JavaFX, OpenGL, or Java interfaces that depend on hardware composition may render blank.
rendering.vnc_wayland_shared: VNC is sharing an existing Wayland desktop
rendering.vnc_wayland_shared_detail: Applications are still rendered by the original desktop session; VNC transmits only the final image.
rendering.vnc_x11_shared: VNC is sharing the existing X11 {{display}}
rendering.vnc_x11_shared_detail: Applications are still rendered by the source X11 session; VNC itself does not convert hardware rendering to software rendering.
rendering.vnc_unknown: The VNC rendering source has not been determined
rendering.vnc_unknown_detail: After the VNC service starts, Terma can determine whether it shares an existing desktop or creates an independent virtual display.
rendering.xdmcp_remote_x11: XDMCP uses the client X Server, so direct GPU rendering is usually limited
rendering.xdmcp_remote_x11_detail: Ordinary X11 interfaces usually work, but JavaFX, OpenGL, JOGL, or embedded browsers may require software-rendering options.

rdp_status.non_linux_title: This host does not use Linux xrdp management
rdp_status.not_installed_title: xrdp not installed on the remote host
rdp_status.non_linux_detail: Terma does not install xrdp on non-Linux hosts. You can still use the system RDP service directly.
rdp_status.install_hint: Choose an available installation method below. Local-download offline installation supports only Debian/Ubuntu and compatible APT/.deb systems.
rdp_status.ssh_management_optional: RDP can use the system service directly. Create and link an SSH management connection to manage Linux xrdp, desktops, and installation status.
rdp_status.standalone_detail: On Windows, enable Remote Desktop in System Settings and allow TCP 3389, or the current custom port. Terma detects the port and launches the local RDP client directly; SSH is not required.
rdp_status.management_link_hint: If the target is Linux and you want Terma to install or manage xrdp, desktop environments, and service status, create an SSH management connection. This does not change the current RDP configuration.
rdp_status.guide_non_linux: The SSH management host is not Linux, so Terma will not install xrdp.
rdp_status.guide_native_server: On Windows, enable Remote Desktop in System Settings. For other systems, follow the documentation for their native RDP server.
rdp_status.guide_desktop: First confirm that a usable Linux desktop is installed remotely. If not, open Linux desktop management to install XFCE, GNOME, Plasma, or another desktop environment.
rdp_status.guide_install: Install xrdp and its Xorg backend, then enable the xrdp service for the distribution.
rdp_status.guide_firewall: Open TCP 3389 only when an active firewall is detected and the port is not already allowed. No rule is needed when the firewall is disabled.
rdp_status.guide_redetect: After installation, return to the RDP workspace, detect the service again, and launch the local RDP client.
rdp_status.guide_installed: xrdp was detected on the remote host. If connection still fails, check the desktop session, service state, and TCP 3389.
rdp_status.guide_unsupported: This host does not support automatic Linux xrdp installation.
rdp_status.guide_missing: xrdp was not detected on the remote host. Choose an installation method or view the manual instructions.
rdp_status.guide_offline_note: If neither the remote host nor this device can access the network, download xrdp, xorgxrdp, and all dependencies on another device with the same distribution, version, and architecture, then upload and install them remotely.
rdp_status.guide_read_failed: Failed to read the RDP installation guide
rdp_status.task_running: An RDP service task is already running. Wait for it to finish.
rdp_status.confirm_local_offline_install: For a detected Debian/Ubuntu or compatible APT/.deb system, Terma will download xrdp packages and dependencies for the matching architecture locally, upload them through SFTP, and install them remotely. Continue?
rdp_status.confirm_remote_cache_install: Terma will install xrdp only from packages already cached by the remote package manager, without accessing repositories. Installation will fail if the cache is incomplete. Continue?
rdp_status.confirm_online_install: Terma will install xrdp and its Xorg backend from the remote package repositories. Continue?
rdp_status.ssh_management_missing: This RDP connection has no linked SSH management connection
rdp_status.install_queued: RDP service installation was added to Task Center
rdp_status.install_complete_redetected: RDP service installation completed; remote status inspected again
rdp_status.install_failed: Failed to install the RDP service ({{mode}})
rdp_status.confirm_uninstall: This will stop and remove remote xrdp and its Xorg backend. The desktop environment will remain installed, but active RDP sessions will disconnect immediately. Continue?
rdp_status.confirm_stop: This will stop the remote xrdp service and immediately disconnect active RDP sessions. Continue?
rdp_status.confirm_restart: This will restart the remote xrdp service and immediately disconnect active RDP sessions. Continue?
rdp_status.confirm_start: This will enable and start the remote xrdp service. Continue?

vnc_status.failure_refused: The remote host refused the connection to port 5900; the VNC service may not be enabled yet.
vnc_status.failure_timeout: The connection to remote port 5900 timed out. Check both the network and firewall.
vnc_status.failure_resolve: The remote host address could not be resolved. Check the connection address.
vnc_status.ssh_management_optional: VNC connects by port and RFB first. Link SSH to manage Linux VNC services and graphical sessions.
vnc_status.accessible_title: VNC service is accessible, but the connection did not complete
vnc_status.accessible_summary: The remote VNC port is accessible. Check the authentication method and connection password.
vnc_status.macos_disabled_title: macOS Screen Sharing is not enabled
vnc_status.macos_disabled_summary: macOS includes a VNC service. Enable Screen Sharing or Remote Management in System Settings.
vnc_status.not_installed_summary: No VNC Server component was detected on the remote Linux host. You can authorize Terma to install it or follow the manual instructions.
vnc_status.stopped_title: VNC service installed but not started
vnc_status.stopped_summary: A VNC component or service unit exists on the remote host, but the target port is not listening. Try starting the service or open the manual setup guide.
vnc_status.blocked_title: The VNC service may be blocked by a firewall
vnc_status.blocked_summary: A VNC component was detected remotely, but the target port is not reachable from the current network. Check the firewall and security groups.
vnc_status.not_listening_title: VNC service is not listening on the target port
vnc_status.not_listening_summary: A remote VNC component exists but is not listening on the port configured for this connection. The display number or service configuration may not match.
vnc_status.probe_unavailable_title: Remote VNC service detection could not finish
vnc_status.probe_unavailable_summary: The SSH management connection is temporarily unavailable, so Terma cannot distinguish an uninstalled service from a stopped one. You can open the manual installation/setup guide first.
vnc_status.probe_unavailable_connection_summary: Terma does not use a bare TCP probe as a VNC connection. SSH inspection is unavailable, so this does not prove that port 5900 is closed. Check the VNC authentication method and password, then retry.
vnc_status.connection_failed_title: The VNC connection did not complete
vnc_status.connection_failed_summary: The remote side closed or rejected Terma during the VNC/RFB handshake. Common causes are an unsupported authentication method, an incorrect password, or a server-side client restriction. Check the password and retry.
vnc_status.connection_failed_with_detail: The remote server returned: “{{detail}}”. Check the VNC server status, failure blacklist, and connection password before retrying.
vnc_status.unsupported_security_title: The built-in VNC client does not support this authentication
vnc_status.unsupported_security_summary: This RealVNC server offered authentication types ({{types}}) that Terma's built-in client does not support. Use the system VNC Viewer, or enable standard VNC password authentication on the server.
vnc_status.too_many_security_failures_title: The remote side is temporarily rejecting Terma
vnc_status.too_many_security_failures_summary: The remote server returned Too many security failures, which means its failure counter has been triggered. Terma stopped retrying. Wait for the server restriction to clear or use the system VNC Viewer instead.
vnc_status.readonly_source_help: The current VNC service is managed by a system unit. Terma will not rewrite its DISPLAY; change the system service configuration first if you need to switch.
vnc_status.process_source_unknown: A VNC process was detected, but its source is unknown
vnc_status.no_running_desktop: No VNC desktop is currently running
vnc_status.source_auto: Select automatically (when exactly one desktop is active)
vnc_status.multiple_sources: Multiple active graphical desktops were detected. Choose a physical desktop, XRDP session, or independent virtual desktop; Terma will not guess.
vnc_status.component_manual_only: {{component}} requires manual configuration before it can be used.
vnc_status.component_install_required: Install {{component}} for the selected desktop source first.
vnc_status.selected_display_missing: The selected display {{display}} does not currently exist
vnc_status.select_active_display: Select an active display to share
vnc_status.source_help: Physical desktops and XRDP sessions are mirrored by x11vnc. A TigerVNC independent virtual desktop creates a new X11 session and normally uses software rendering. The selection is saved and takes effect the next time the VNC service starts or restarts.
vnc_status.selection_pending_title: The selected desktop source has not taken effect
vnc_status.selection_pending_summary: The current VNC service is still using the old source. Apply the source and restart, or install the component required by the target source first.
vnc_status.ready_summary: The remote VNC port and service checks passed. You can open the remote desktop.
vnc_status.macos_settings_path: System Settings > General > Sharing > Screen Sharing
vnc_status.macos_step_enable: Enable either Screen Sharing or Remote Management.
vnc_status.macos_step_account: Open the details and add the macOS account used by this connection under Allow access.
vnc_status.macos_step_password: For built-in VNC, allow VNC viewers to control the screen with a password, set that password, and save it in Connection settings.
vnc_status.macos_legacy_path: Older macOS: System Preferences > Sharing > Screen Sharing
vnc_status.check_items_value: VNC service · TCP {{port}} · firewall · connection password
vnc_status.managed_persistent: Managed by Terma · starts automatically after restart
vnc_status.reenter_embedded_title: Re-enter the built-in VNC desktop that is still running
vnc_status.embedded_running: The built-in VNC desktop is still running; you can re-enter or close it
vnc_status.embedded_disconnected: The built-in VNC desktop is disconnected; you can re-enter or close it
vnc_status.source_save_failed: Failed to save the VNC desktop source

xdmcp_status.warning_macos: macOS does not provide an XDMCP graphical login service that Terma can configure. Use VNC to share the desktop or SSH X11 to open individual graphical applications.
xdmcp_status.warning_privilege: The current SSH management account does not have root or passwordless sudo access. Use the action button to enter a one-time administrator account, password, private key, or SSH Agent, or run the command manually in a terminal.
xdmcp_status.warning_local_conflict: Account {{user}} is already running Plasma on the local desktop ({{display}}). Another XDMCP login with the same account may show only the wallpaper. Sign out of the local desktop or use another account.
xdmcp_status.warning_remote_conflict: {{count}} remote graphical sessions for the same account were detected, and Plasma is still bound to {{display}}. End those sessions before starting a new XDMCP desktop.
xdmcp_status.warning_root_plasma: The current account starts Plasma X11 as root. KDE sessions can render blank because of DBus/KDE runtime conflicts. Install and switch to a lightweight X11 session such as XFCE, or use a regular desktop account.
xdmcp_status.warning_no_desktop_listening: XDMCP is enabled and UDP 177 is listening, but the remote host has no X11 desktop session it can start. Direct login will usually produce a blank screen. Install XFCE, Plasma X11, or another X11 desktop first.
xdmcp_status.warning_no_desktop_enabled: The XDMCP configuration is written, but UDP 177 is not listening and the remote host has no startable X11 desktop session. Install a desktop, then apply the configuration and restart the display manager.
xdmcp_status.warning_no_desktop_disabled: XDMCP is disabled, UDP 177 is not listening, and the remote host has no startable X11 desktop session. Install a desktop, then enable the XDMCP service.
xdmcp_status.warning_session_repair: The desktop session {{session}} saved for the management account cannot start a complete desktop. Terma can change it automatically to {{preferred}}.
xdmcp_status.warning_sddm: The current SDDM does not provide an XDMCP server. On Debian/Ubuntu, you can install and switch to LightDM.
xdmcp_status.warning_gdm: The current GDM{{version}} does not provide a usable XDMCP server. GDM 50 and later removed this capability; on Debian/Ubuntu, you can install and switch to LightDM.
xdmcp_status.warning_manager_unsupported: Terma cannot automatically configure the current display manager.
xdmcp_status.security_warning: XDMCP is unencrypted and should be used only on a trusted LAN.
xdmcp_status.probe_unavailable_launch_anyway: Full SSH inspection is unavailable, but you can still try the XDMCP graphical login directly
xdmcp_status.configured_restart_pending: XDMCP configured · waiting for display-manager restart
xdmcp_status.pending_restart: The X11 desktop session and display manager {{manager}} are ready. The XDMCP configuration is written, but UDP 177 is not listening; apply it and restart the display manager.
xdmcp_status.pending_enable: The X11 desktop session and display manager {{manager}} are ready. Only the XDMCP service needs to be enabled; the desktop and display manager do not need to be reinstalled or switched.
xdmcp_status.saved_desktop_title: Default desktop saved for the management account
xdmcp_status.macos_no_session: macOS does not provide an XDMCP X11 desktop session.
xdmcp_status.no_login_session: No X11 desktop session available for XDMCP login was detected; direct login may show a blank screen.
xdmcp_status.client_required: Install or start the local XDMCP client first
xdmcp_status.not_safe_to_start: Remote XDMCP is not currently safe to start
xdmcp_status.ssh_management_optional: You can try an XDMCP graphical login directly. Link SSH to inspect and manage the display manager, desktop sessions, and UDP 177 service.

xdmcp_setup.no_auto_command: No installation command can be run automatically. Follow the manual instructions.
xdmcp_setup.shell_install_complete: XDMCP dependency installation finished. Press Enter to return to the shell.
xdmcp_setup.no_copy_command: There is no installation command to copy
xdmcp_setup.standalone_detail: The target Linux host must enable an XDMCP-capable display manager and allow UDP 177. XDMCP is unencrypted and should be used only on a trusted LAN. Terma can attempt a graphical login directly without SSH.
xdmcp_setup.management_link_hint: After SSH is linked, Terma can detect the display manager and desktop sessions and provide installation, enablement, repair, and firewall configuration.
xdmcp_setup.step_macos_no_manager: A remote macOS host has no XDMCP display manager that Terma can enable automatically. Use XDMCP on a Linux server; use VNC for a macOS server.
xdmcp_setup.step_macos_xquartz: To run individual X11 applications, install and start XQuartz locally, then use SSH X11 forwarding.
xdmcp_setup.step_desktop_required: XDMCP only sends the login screen to the local device. The remote host must also have a usable X11 desktop session installed.
xdmcp_setup.step_root_plasma: The current account is root and uses Plasma. KDE/DBus runtime conflicts can produce a blank screen; install and switch to XFCE.
xdmcp_setup.step_redetect_launch: After installation, return to this page, click Detect again, and start the graphical login.
xdmcp_setup.step_udp_firewall: XDMCP uses UDP 177. Allow 177/UDP in the firewall only on a trusted LAN.
xdmcp_setup.step_manager_missing: The current desktop session is usable, but the existing display manager does not provide a usable XDMCP server.
xdmcp_setup.step_switch_lightdm: On Debian/Ubuntu, Terma can install and switch to LightDM. This ends the current graphical login, so save your work first.
xdmcp_setup.step_redetect_after_switch: After switching, detect again and start the graphical login.
xdmcp_setup.step_trusted_lan: XDMCP uses UDP 177 and should be enabled only on a trusted LAN.
xdmcp_setup.step_ready: {{manager}} and {{desktop}} are ready, and the remote host is listening on UDP 177.
xdmcp_setup.step_ready_launch: Close this guide and start a new graphical login. LightDM and the desktop environment do not need to be installed again.
xdmcp_setup.step_components_ready: {{manager}} and {{desktop}} were detected; the desktop components are ready.
xdmcp_setup.step_enable_only: Only the XDMCP service switch is missing. Return to the connection page and click Enable XDMCP service; do not reinstall LightDM or the desktop environment.
xdmcp_setup.step_firewall_behavior: When enabling XDMCP, Terma opens UDP 177 only if an active firewall is detected. It does not add unnecessary rules when no firewall is enabled.
xdmcp_setup.step_confirm_manager: Confirm that a remote display manager and an X11 desktop session are installed.
xdmcp_setup.step_install_or_enable: If components are missing, install a desktop or switch the display manager. If all components are present, only enable the XDMCP service.
xdmcp_setup.step_redetect: After the operation, return to this page and click Detect again.
xdmcp_setup.enabled_listening: XDMCP is enabled and the remote host is listening on UDP 177.
xdmcp_setup.configured_not_listening: The XDMCP configuration is written, but UDP 177 is not listening. Apply the configuration and restart the display manager.
xdmcp_setup.manager_ready_disabled: {{manager}} is installed and configurable, but XDMCP is disabled and UDP 177 is not listening.
xdmcp_setup.service_not_detected: No usable XDMCP/UDP 177 service is currently detected.
xdmcp_setup.admin_install_note: Temporary administrator authorization is used only for this operation. Installing or switching the display manager may end the current graphical session. When XDMCP is enabled, a UDP 177 rule is added only if an active firewall is detected.
xdmcp_setup.run_reference_terminal: Run reference commands in a terminal
xdmcp_setup.guide_read_failed: Failed to read the XDMCP installation guide
xdmcp_setup.progress_switch_xfce: Switching to a separate XFCE session
xdmcp_setup.progress_wait_notice: This operation may take several minutes. Do not close Terma or the remote terminal.
xdmcp_setup.task_running: An XDMCP service task is already running. Wait for it to finish.
xdmcp_setup.confirm_cleanup_sessions: The same Linux account already has an XRDP/XDMCP graphical session, and Plasma remains bound to the old display. Only remote graphical sessions without a local seat will be ended; the seat0 local desktop will remain open. Unsaved remote-desktop content will be lost.
xdmcp_setup.confirm_repair_session: The invalid or generic desktop session saved for the current SSH management account will be changed to the automatically detected X11 desktop, and LightDM will restart. The current local graphical session will end.

xdmcp_setup.confirm_install_rdp: Use {{mode}}{{suffix}} to install xrdp and its Xorg backend. After installation, detect again and inspect the RDP desktop session.
xdmcp_setup.confirm_repair_xrdp: The remote xrdp startup script will be backed up and changed to use a separate XFCE session after cleaning the old D-Bus environment. Existing RDP sessions will restart.
xdmcp_setup.confirm_disable: This will disable XDMCP and restart the graphical login service. The current local graphical session may end.
xdmcp_setup.confirm_enable: The display-manager configuration will be backed up, XDMCP will be enabled, and the graphical login service will restart immediately. The current local graphical session will end and unsaved content may be lost.

clipboard_guide.macos_summary: macOS includes pbcopy and pbpaste. Terma does not install Linux clipboard packages such as xclip, xsel, or wl-clipboard on macOS.
clipboard_guide.macos_confirm_connection: Confirm that the SSH helper connection uses the same macOS host and account as this VNC session.
clipboard_guide.macos_confirm_session: Confirm that the account is signed in to the macOS graphical desktop. The system clipboard may be unavailable to a background-only SSH session.
clipboard_guide.macos_verify_tools: Run /usr/bin/pbcopy and /usr/bin/pbpaste in a terminal to verify that the account can read and write the system clipboard.
clipboard_guide.macos_relogin: If the commands exist but clipboard access still fails, sign out of the graphical desktop, sign in again, and detect again in Terma.

clipboard_guide.linux_install_tool: Install xclip or xsel for an X11 session, or wl-clipboard for a Wayland session.
clipboard_guide.linux_session_environment: The SSH helper account must be able to access the active graphical session and must have the correct DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR environment.
clipboard_guide.linux_redetect: After installation, return to Terma and detect again. The VNC connection does not need to be recreated.
clipboard_guide.linux_offline_apt: For Debian, Ubuntu, and compatible APT/.deb systems, choose Local offline when the remote host has no network access. If this device is also offline, prepare the packages according to the distribution documentation and install them manually.

vnc_guide.macos_summary: macOS includes Screen Sharing/VNC, so no separate VNC Server installation is required.
vnc_guide.macos_enable_sharing: Turn on Screen Sharing and allow the macOS account used by this connection in the details.
vnc_guide.macos_password: To use a VNC password, open the Screen Sharing access settings, enable password access for VNC viewers, and set the password.
vnc_guide.macos_redetect: Return to Terma and inspect TCP {{port}} again. If it is still unreachable, check the macOS firewall and local-network permissions.
vnc_guide.unknown_summary: This VNC connection has no usable SSH management channel, so Terma cannot identify the remote system or tell whether the service is missing or stopped.
vnc_guide.unknown_link_ssh: Link an SSH connection for the same host in Connection Settings to enable read-only inspection and temporarily authorized installation.
vnc_guide.unknown_check_port: You can also check manually on the remote host whether a VNC Server is listening on TCP {{port}}.
vnc_guide.unknown_platform_help: On macOS, enable Screen Sharing or Remote Management under System Settings > General > Sharing. On Linux, install x11vnc or TigerVNC with the distribution package manager.
vnc_guide.linux_title: Linux VNC service installation and configuration
vnc_guide.linux_component_install_required: {{component}} is not fully installed. Install the complete component before configuring and starting it.
vnc_guide.linux_installed_stopped: {{component}} was detected, but the current port has no usable listener. Terma can configure and start it, or you can run the reference commands manually.
vnc_guide.linux_installed_manual: {{component}} was detected, but no safe automatic start plan is available. Configure it with the reference commands below.
vnc_guide.linux_component_missing: {{component}} was not detected on this host. Install it with temporary administrator authorization or from a terminal.
vnc_guide.linux_session_missing: No reusable active graphical session was detected. For an independent desktop, use TigerVNC together with Linux Desktop Management.
vnc_guide.linux_install_tigervnc_manual: Only the raw Xtigervnc/Xvnc server is available, without a vncserver/tigervncserver wrapper. Install the complete TigerVNC Server or manually create the X session, window manager, and authentication configuration for this distribution.
vnc_guide.linux_install_tigervnc: After installing the complete TigerVNC Server and clipboard helpers, run vncpasswd for the target account, then use vncserver to create an independent desktop session.
vnc_guide.linux_install_x11vnc: After installing x11vnc and clipboard helpers, run x11vnc -storepasswd to create the VNC password file. Terma creates it automatically only when a VNC password has been saved in Connection Settings.
vnc_guide.linux_virtual_session: An independent virtual desktop does not depend on the current physical screen or XRDP session. Confirm that a Linux desktop start command is available and retain the target account's ~/.vnc configuration.
vnc_guide.linux_shared_session: Start x11vnc on the existing graphical desktop and confirm that DISPLAY={{display}} and XAUTHORITY point to that desktop.
vnc_guide.linux_redetect: Confirm that the service is listening on TCP {{port}}, then inspect it again in Terma.
vnc_guide.linux_clipboard: Linux X11 clipboard integration requires xclip/xsel; Wayland requires wl-clipboard. Without these tools, Terma keeps manual synchronization available and does not replace Chinese text with question marks.
